- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5) — adjust forecast to align with sentiment mean, not extreme highs/lows.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.1) and price is stable, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid “flat” bias.
- When sentiment is high but price is declining, model often ignores sentiment — force a slight downward correction (–0.5% to –1.5%) to reflect sentiment divergence.
